newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian MTBE - Steady, unlikely to follow U.S. plunge.
newsitem.headline: Asian MTBE - Steady, unlikely to follow U.S. plunge.

text.p: Asian spot MTBE prices were steady to firm but were unlikely to follow the tumble in U.S. spot prices, traders said on Wednesday.
"Prices in the U.S. weakened quite a bit and buyers will try to push price here down," said one MTBE supplier. "But supply is the same and I don't think prices here will drop in the same magnitude."

Ample supplies and plunging NYMEX gasoline futures pressured down prices in the U.S. last week. By last Thursday, New York MTBE prices had fallen in a week by about 7.50 cents per gallon to 82.00/83.00 cents while Houston prices in the Gulf coast dropped five cents to 77.75/78.75 cents.
"When prices there rise, prices here don't necessarily rise and vice versa. We are serving the Asian market," said another supplier.
Asian spot prices were stable to firm with 1,000 tonnes in March sold last week by a Mideast supplier to a U.S. major at $285 per tonne on a cost-and-freight basis Singapore.
"That is slightly lower than I would sell," said another supplier. "March is not under pressure, there is not that much cargo."

Sellers raised their quotes for March supplies to $285-$290 per tonne on a cost-and-freight Singapore basis and $275-$278 free-on-board, compared to last Wednesday's respective quotes at $280-$289 and $270-$275.
But buyers were quiet amidst New Year holidays while regional demand has mostly been covered. Only around 1,500 tonnes were still being sought into Thailand, traders said.

Traders looked to Taiwan for fresh demand. Taiwan issued a new tender for reformate for second-half March delivery and was expected to buy more cargoes with a 2.0-percent MTBE requirement after its disappointing purchase of only one cargo for the first half. The tender closes February 18 and is valid until February 20.
